suburbs.name: Morphett Vale
suburbs.blurb: The largest suburb on our Adelaide list, in the established southern suburbs.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, AFL, netball and cricket are the main sports at southern clubs and schools.
suburbs.occasion: junior club presentations and school awards across the south
suburbs.fact: It is close to the McLaren Vale wine region.

suburbs.name: Parafield Gardens
suburbs.blurb: A large northern suburb with a long-settled community and busy local clubs.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, AFL, netball and basketball fill the northern calendar.
suburbs.occasion: community club awards and school sports days

suburbs.name: Mount Barker
suburbs.blurb: The main centre of the Adelaide Hills and one of South Australia's fastest-growing districts.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and equestrian events are the mainstays of Hills clubs.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball presentations and pony club and show days

suburbs.name: Paralowie
suburbs.blurb: A family suburb in the City of Salisbury, with many young families and local schools.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, AFL, basketball and netball are popular with Paralowie clubs and schools.
suburbs.occasion: school presentation days and junior club awards

suburbs.name: Prospect
suburbs.blurb: Home to our showroom on Prospect Road, in the inner north just minutes from the CBD.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, cricket, tennis and netball are strong in the inner north.
suburbs.occasion: club and school presentations across the inner north
suburbs.fact: Prospect Oval is home to the North Adelaide Football Club.

suburbs.name: Mawson Lakes
suburbs.blurb: A planned suburb built around its lakes, with a university campus and a mix of students and families.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, cricket and basketball sit alongside university and school awards.
suburbs.occasion: school awards, university sport and junior club presentations
suburbs.fact: The University of South Australia has a campus at Mawson Lakes.

suburbs.name: Hallett Cove
suburbs.blurb: A coastal southern suburb on Gulf St Vincent, known for its cliffs and beaches.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, netball, soccer and sailing feature in local club life.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball presentations and sailing club awards
suburbs.fact: Hallett Cove Conservation Park and its sculpture trail are local landmarks.

suburbs.name: Happy Valley
suburbs.blurb: A well-established southern suburb in the City of Onkaparinga, with large schools and sporting clubs.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, AFL, cricket and golf are the busiest local sports.
suburbs.occasion: school sports awards and golf day presentations

suburbs.name: Woodcroft
suburbs.blurb: A family suburb in the south with many young households and neighbourhood clubs.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, netball, AFL and tennis are popular with Woodcroft families.
suburbs.occasion: junior club presentations and school tennis and netball awards

suburbs.name: Aldinga Beach
suburbs.blurb: A growing coastal suburb on the Fleurieu side of the metro area, with a seaside lifestyle.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and fishing suit the coastal community.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball presentations and fishing club competitions

drive.route: the Southern Expressway (M2) and Main South Road

suburbs.name: Athelstone
suburbs.blurb: A leafy foothills suburb in the north-east, backing onto the hills.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, cricket, netball and tennis are all well supported in the north-east.
suburbs.occasion: club presentation nights and school sport awards

suburbs.name: Andrews Farm
suburbs.blurb: A younger suburb in the City of Playford, in Adelaide's growing outer north.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, AFL, basketball and netball are the main sports for local families.
suburbs.occasion: junior club presentations and school awards

suburbs.name: Aberfoyle Park
suburbs.blurb: A large, settled suburb in the south, with plenty of schools and sporting facilities.
suburbs.sportline: Netball, soccer, tennis and basketball are strong across Aberfoyle Park.
suburbs.occasion: school sports awards and netball association presentations

suburbs.name: Salisbury North
suburbs.blurb: An established northern suburb in the City of Salisbury, with long-running community clubs.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, soccer, cricket and athletics are staples of the local calendar.
suburbs.occasion: community club awards, athletics carnivals and school sports days

suburbs.name: Seaford
suburbs.blurb: A coastal southern suburb on the edge of the metro area, close to the beach.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, soccer, netball and fishing suit Seaford's community clubs.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball presentations and fishing competitions

suburbs.name: Munno Para
suburbs.blurb: A growing outer northern suburb in the City of Playford, close to Gawler.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, soccer, basketball and cricket are the main sports for local clubs.
suburbs.occasion: junior club presentations and school sports awards

suburbs.name: North Adelaide
suburbs.blurb: A historic inner suburb on the northern edge of the CBD, with a strong mix of residents, schools and businesses.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, cricket, tennis and rowing on the Torrens lead the local sporting year.
suburbs.occasion: school and club presentations and corporate recognition
suburbs.fact: Adelaide Oval sits on the edge of North Adelaide.

suburbs.name: Henley Beach
suburbs.blurb: A beachside suburb on the western coast, centred on Henley Square.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, netball, fishing and swimming suit the seaside community.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball presentations and swimming club awards
suburbs.fact: Henley Square sits right on the beachfront.

suburbs.name: Gawler
suburbs.pop_text: more than 20,000 residents across its wider area
suburbs.blurb: An outer northern growth hub and the gateway to the Barossa, with its own town centre.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and equestrian events fill the Gawler calendar.
suburbs.occasion: football-netball presentations, pony club days and school awards

towns.name: Victor Harbor–Goolwa
towns.blurb: A popular coastal region on the Fleurieu Peninsula, taking in Victor Harbor and Goolwa near the Murray mouth.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, sailing and fishing reflect life on the Fleurieu coast.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, sailing club awards and fishing competitions
towns.fact: The horse-drawn tram to Granite Island is Victor Harbor's best-known attraction.

towns.name: Mount Gambier
towns.blurb: The regional capital of the Limestone Coast, in South Australia's south-east near the Victorian border.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, soccer and basketball anchor the local sporting calendar.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and school sports days
towns.fact: The Blue Lake and Umpherston Sinkhole are well-known local attractions.

towns.name: Whyalla
towns.blurb: A steel city on the Spencer Gulf in the state's mid-north, and the largest centre in the upper gulf.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, fishing and soccer are the main sports across the upper gulf.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and fishing club competitions
towns.fact: The giant Australian cuttlefish gather each winter nearby at Point Lowly.

towns.name: Murray Bridge
towns.blurb: The main town of the Murraylands, built around the Murray River east of the Adelaide Hills.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, rowing and fishing make full use of the river.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, rowing regattas and fishing competitions

towns.name: Port Lincoln
towns.blurb: The seafood capital of the Eyre Peninsula, on Boston Bay at the tip of the peninsula.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, fishing and sailing reflect Port Lincoln's life on the water.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, sailing regattas and fishing club awards
towns.fact: The annual Tunarama Festival celebrates the local tuna industry.

drive.route: the Princes Highway (A1) and Lincoln Highway (B100)

towns.name: Port Pirie
towns.blurb: A port city at the head of the Spencer Gulf, in the state's mid-north.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and lawn bowls are the mainstays of local clubs.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and lawn bowls pennant awards

towns.name: Port Augusta
towns.blurb: A crossroads city at the head of the Spencer Gulf and the gateway to the Flinders Ranges and the outback.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and soccer anchor the local sporting year.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and school sports days
towns.fact: The Australian Arid Lands Botanic Garden is in Port Augusta.
